description: The browser's own <select>, styled as the Monark pill trigger. It keeps every native behaviour (OS picker on phones, type-ahead, form submission, works without JS), so there is no custom ARIA. The native arrow is hidden with appearance-none and an aria-hidden chevron is drawn inside the right padding instead.

keyboard.action: Moves focus to and from the select.
Changes the selected option (or opens the picker, depending on the platform).
Typing jumps to the first option starting with those characters.

focus.notes: focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50 with focus-visible:border-ring, the same ring as SelectTrigger. The control is h-10 (sm h-9) and grows to h-11 (44px) on coarse pointers, since a <select> can't carry an ::after hit area.

announcements: Announced natively as a combo box / pop-up button with its label and current value.
screenReader.notes: The chevron is aria-hidden; everything else is the platform's own semantics. aria-invalid and aria-describedby on NativeSelect are passed to the <select> itself.

contrast.text: Value text uses foreground on bg-card; meets WCAG AA. Options use popover / popover-foreground where the browser honours option styling
contrast.ui: Border uses the input token (3.9:1); meets AA non-text contrast. The invalid state switches to the destructive border plus ring

motion.reducedMotion: Only a colour transition on hover; the picker itself is drawn by the OS

consumerResponsibilities: Label it with a <Label htmlFor> (or aria-label for a toolbar filter); a select without a name is announced as an unnamed combo box.
Note that className goes on the wrapper (use it for width); all other props, including id and aria-*, go on the <select>.
Prefer the Radix Select when options need icons, descriptions or custom rendering; the native picker shows plain text only.
